Nymphaeaceae.key_door: rooted rhizomatous aquatic + long-petioled broad leaves attached at basal sinus + many-stamen solitary flowers; Nymphaea vs Nuphar by flower/venation architecture

Nelumbonaceae.key_door: centrally peltate leaves + emergent flower + separate carpels embedded in enlarged showerhead receptacle

Ceratophyllaceae.key_door: rootless fully submerged shoot + whorled forked denticulate leaves + tiny perianthless flowers + one-seeded spiny achene

taxonomy_notes: Nuphar lutea subsp. advena is a synonym of accepted Nuphar advena under current Kew.
Nymphaea odorata, Nelumbo lutea, and Ceratophyllum demersum remain accepted current concepts.
Current native-range treatments include Texas for Nuphar advena, Nymphaea odorata, Nelumbo lutea, and Ceratophyllum demersum.

guardrails: Family/genus recognition only; no species promotion.
Do not group lotus with water-lilies because of habitat alone; Nelumbo is Proteales, not Nymphaeales.
Do not call the lotus seedhead one capsule; it is an enlarged receptacle holding separate nutlike fruits.
Do not confuse Ceratophyllum 'hornwort' with bryophyte hornworts.
